clue.text: Wave flag for cake

parts.note: to flap is to wave, as a flag or arms do
a jack is a ship's flag, as in Union Jack

explanation.surface: Someone waves a flag in exchange for a slice of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A flapjack is a chewy oat bar in Britain (a pancake in America), either way a baked treat.

clue.text: Data about Eastern aspects

indicators.note: about means the word for data goes around the letter for Eastern

parts.note: data are facts

explanation.surface: Information concerning sides of Eastern life.
explanation.definitionFit: Facets are the sides or features of a subject, so they are its aspects.

clue.text: A disease found around outskirts of Peshawar is roughly reduced

indicators.note: found around means the disease word wraps the outer letters

parts.note: pox is a disease, such as smallpox

indicators.note: the first and last letters of Peshawar are taken as its edges

explanation.surface: An illness around the edge of a Pakistani city has been roughly cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly reduced' is the abbreviated form of approximately: roughly, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Approx is the shortened form of approximately, a word meaning roughly, cut short.

clue.text: Trousers Juliet intends to take top off

parts.note: Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: taking the top off a down entry removes its first letter

parts.note: to mean something is to intend it

explanation.surface: Juliet plans to strip off her top while wearing trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeans are casual denim trousers, an example of the garment.

clue.text: Clot, prisoner and American lass taking drug

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: taking means the girl word holds the letter for the drug

parts.note: gal is an informal, chiefly American word for a girl
E is the slang abbreviation for ecstasy

explanation.surface: An idiot, a convict and a girl from the States get involved with drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' reads as an idiot; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To congeal is to thicken and set, as blood does when it clots.

clue.text: Curse in middle of rubbish day

indicators.note: the central letter of the seven-letter word rubbish is taken

parts.note: daylight, or simply light, is the day as opposed to night

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a curse falling on bin collection day.
explanation.definitionFit: A blight is a plague or affliction that spoils things, close in sense to a curse.

clue.text: Number taking part in strange trial by entrance to Hampton maze

indicators.note: taking part in means the letter for number enters the jumble
strange signals that trial by is rearranged oddly

parts.note: N is the mathematical abbreviation for number

indicators.note: the first letter of Hampton is its way in

explanation.surface: Someone goes into a strange trial near the gates of Hampton maze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges TRIALBY to LABYRIT; N goes in to give LABYRINT. Hampton Court Palace near London has a famous hedge maze.
explanation.definitionFit: A labyrinth is an intricate network of paths, a puzzle of passages like a maze.

clue.text: Help artist upset in piece for newspaper

indicators.note: in means the reversed help-and-artist letters sit inside the word for piece

parts.note: piece is slang for a gun

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the help and artist words upside down

parts.note: aid means help
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist gets upset about helping with a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses AIDRA to ARDIA, which goes inside GUN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Guardian is a British national daily paper.

clue.text: Politicians adopting male opinions

indicators.note: adopting means the politicians word takes the male word inside

parts.note: Tories are Conservative politicians in Britain
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: Politicians take on a man's views.
explanation.definitionFit: Theories are ideas or views held about something, synonyms for opinions.

clue.text: Controls unexpected panic at start of skirmish

indicators.note: unexpected suggests the letters of panic at turn up in a surprising order
the first letter of skirmish is taken

explanation.surface: Panic breaks out unexpectedly as a skirmish begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To captain a team or ship is to control or lead it; the verb sense, third person singular.

clue.text: A British lounge is brightly lit

parts.note: to laze is to lounge about idly

explanation.surface: A British living room is described as brightly lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ablaze is on fire or glowing, so it is lit up brightly.

clue.text: Knock worthless piano

parts.note: bum is slang for worthless or useless, as in a bum deal
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone criticises a useless piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A bump is a blow or collision, so it is a knock.

clue.text: Hole in strap met with audible expression of surprise in bridal store

indicators.note: in means the hole letter is placed inside the strap word

parts.note: a truss is a supporting strap or belt, as for a hernia
O is a hole by its shape

indicators.note: audible tells us to take the sound of the surprised word, not its spelling

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise; it sounds like French eau

explanation.surface: A torn strap prompts a gasp of surprise among a bride's things.
explanation.walkthrough: EAU is French for water, chosen only because it is pronounced like the exclamation; a truss here is a surgical support belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the collection of clothes and linen a bride gathers for married life, a store kept for the wedding.

clue.text: Invader taking out a horseman

indicators.note: taking out means the letter a is removed from the word for invader

parts.note: a raider is someone who invades or attacks

explanation.surface: An invader kills a man on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is anyone who rides, in particular one mounted on a horse.

clue.text: Poster beginning to blog badly

indicators.note: the opening letter of blog is taken

parts.note: ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Someone who posts online starts writing a blog poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poster' looks like someone posting on a blog; it is a printed notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a printed notice stuck up in public, as in 'stick no bills'.

clue.text: Considered perfect agreement is initially exposed in papers

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the word for papers

parts.note: ID means identity papers
a deal is an agreement

indicators.note: the first letter of exposed is taken

explanation.surface: An ideal agreement is first revealed in the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To idealise something is to regard it as perfect, so idealised means thought flawless.

clue.text: Alias of northern bloke returning to be embraced by number one

indicators.note: being embraced by means the reversed piece goes inside the word for number one

parts.note: number one is a childish euphemism for a pee

indicators.note: returning means the letters for northern bloke are read backwards

parts.note: a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A northern bloke comes back to be hugged by the top person, under an assumed name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' is nursery talk for urinating, the polite counterpart of number two; it is not the boss the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen name is a pseudonym used by a writer, so it is an alias.

clue.text: Rumours of about 20 lost in terrible shipwrecks

indicators.note: lost means these named letters are dropped from the fodder
terrible suggests the remaining letters of the fodder are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
20-down is KING, and K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Talk of about twenty lost in dreadful shipwrecks.
explanation.walkthrough: Take C and K (from 20-down, KING) out of SHIPWRECKS and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Whispers are hushed rumours passed along, as in whispers of a takeover.

clue.text: A Parisian left dreadful criminal

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it
awful means dreadful

explanation.surface: A Parisian departs, a dreadful crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlawful breaks the law, the adjective criminal.

clue.text: Female to kiss nag

parts.note: a hen is a female bird, and informally a woman
a peck is a quick kiss

explanation.surface: A woman goes in for a kiss with an old horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nag' looks like a horse; it is the verb to keep on at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To henpeck is to keep criticising and bossing a partner, the verb to nag.

clue.text: Family joined by good man

parts.note: kin are family or relatives

explanation.surface: A family is joined by a decent man.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, the pieces are called men, and the king is the most important of them.

clue.text: Hard to get into club in foreign capital

indicators.note: getting into means the letter for hard goes inside the word for club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games such as cricket
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Getting into a nightclub in a foreign capital city is tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' means money here, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The baht is the currency of Thailand, so foreign money or capital.

clue.text: Most of earth consuming Italian food

indicators.note: consuming means the shortened word swallows the Italian letters
most of means the last letter of the burrow word is dropped

parts.note: an earth is a burrow, as a fox's earth

explanation.surface: Most of the world eats Italian cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earth' looks like the planet; it is an animal's burrow. 'Most of' cuts it to BURRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a Mexican dish, a tortilla wrapped round a filling.

clue.text: Opening left wall exposed

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: exposed means the outer letters are stripped from wall, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A gap leaves a wall bare.
explanation.definitionFit: A portal is a doorway or gateway, an opening.

clue.text: Wit of lively priest

indicators.note: lively suggests the letters of priest are jumping about

explanation.surface: A cheerful clergyman is full of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is French for spirit and means lively wit, as in esprit de corps.

clue.text: Start to stick pin into dawdler

indicators.note: the opening letter of stick is taken

parts.note: a nail is a metal pin driven into wood

explanation.surface: Someone begins sticking a pin into a slowcoach.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail moves very slowly, so the word is used for a sluggish person who lags behind.

clue.text: Roar and rant about sons — they tell tales

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son or sons

explanation.surface: Storytellers roar and rant about their children.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrators are people who relate a story, so they tell tales.

clue.text: Goodwill from alternative military institution towards young leaders

indicators.note: leaders means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: An alternative military college shows goodwill to the young.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendship and peaceful relations, a synonym for goodwill.

clue.text: Tricky angle on outside of easel

indicators.note: the outer letters, first and last, of easel are taken

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A painter's tricky corner sits beyond the easel.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfish means like an elf, hence mischievous and impish, which is tricky.

clue.text: Sibling holding in evil

indicators.note: holding means the sibling word contains the word in

parts.note: a sister is a sibling

explanation.surface: A brother or sister is keeping some wickedness inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister describes something threatening harm, a synonym for wicked or malevolent.

clue.text: Meals made by Salvation Army youths

parts.note: lads are young men

explanation.surface: Charity workers serve food to young people.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad can be a whole dish served as a light lunch, so salads are meals.

clue.text: Log typo misprinted including line written in many languages

indicators.note: including means the jumbled letters take in the letter for line
a misprint jumbles the letters of log typo

explanation.surface: A typing error in a log is printed wrongly, with an extra line, in several tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misprinted' shuffles LOGTYPO; 'including' puts L inside that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyglot text, such as a Bible, prints the same work in several languages side by side.
